text:
Buffalo visits Montreal tonight, four days after the Canadiens beat the Sabres 4-3 in a shootout, a game MTL deserved to win 73% of the time. The model has it close, BUF 3.12 expected goals to MTL 3.04. Both teams take 55% of the expected goals at five on five, though Montreal gives up more (3.41 per 60 against Buffalo's 2.84) and has taken 5.6 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opposing power plays. The Canadiens' penalty kill allows 0.83 expected goals a game, worse than Buffalo's 0.72. Dahlin is out for the Sabres and Demidov is on injured reserve for Montreal.

The goalies have both struggled this season. Projected starter Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is at .854 and -4.86 goals saved above expected over six games, while Jakub Dobes is at .841 and -5.54 over four. Last year they were far apart: Dobes was +17.26 over 43 games, Luukkonen +9.12 over 35. Dobes has the longer record of stopping more than he should, but he is the one in worse form now.

Recent form leans slightly toward neither side. Buffalo is 2-2-1 in its last five with 47% of the expected goals, and Montreal is 2-3-0 with 48%. This is also a rematch of last spring's second-round series, which Montreal won in seven, though the model doesn't price that. Tage Thompson has a 41% chance to score and a 66% chance at a point, and Cole Caufield sits at 39% to score. Nick Suzuki's 72% point probability is the highest on the board.
